key_insight: LuxAvatar separates a head avatar’s 3D structure and surface properties from its lighting appearance. This lets a single portrait drive an animatable, relightable avatar using a 3D Gaussian proxy and a neural shader.
problem_solved: Creating real-time head avatars from one portrait while maintaining controllable 3D motion, consistent appearance across viewpoints, and realistic responses to changing lighting.
method: Build an animatable 3D intrinsic Gaussian proxy that separates canonical geometry from reflectance attributes.
Deform and rapidly rasterize the Gaussians into physically based rendering (PBR) buffers that remain consistent across views and motion.
Condition a causal autoregressive neural shader on these buffers to model complex facial light transport.
impact: The approach targets interactive avatars that can be animated and relit without rebuilding their appearance for each scene. It offers practitioners a hybrid design combining explicit 3D control with learned shading; the supplied abstract excerpt does not include quantitative results.
visual_elements: Pipeline: single portrait → 3D Gaussian proxy → PBR buffers → neural shader → rendered avatar.
Layered head illustration separating geometry, reflectance, and final shading.
Same avatar under several lighting directions to demonstrate relighting.
Grid of viewpoints and facial poses illustrating intended view and motion consistency.
paper_title: LuxAvatar: Real-Time Relightable Head Avatars via Causal Neural Shading of 3D Intrinsic Proxies
paper_authors: Yipengjing Sun, Chenyang Wang, Boyao Zhou, Jiapeng Zhu, Ka Leong Cheng
